record.paper_title: Modal logics for metric spaces: open problems
record.original_question: For fragments of MS, determine the satisfiability problem over bounded subspaces of n-dimensional Euclidean space R^n, including spaces such as the unit square [0,1] x [0,1] with the inherited Euclidean metric.

artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an explicit open problem in the literature on modal logics for metric spaces. Related results show that full MS satisfiability over the real line and finite Euclidean subspaces is undecidable, while ExpTime-completeness is known for some abstract distance-space classes; however, no published resolution of decidability/complexity for fragments of MS over bounded Euclidean subspaces such as $[0,1]^2$ was located. Status appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Modal Logics for Metric Spaces: Open Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Listed as an open problem regarding satisfiability of MS fragments over bounded Euclidean subspaces.
status_evidence.claim: The question is posed as an open problem in the surveyed literature on modal logics for metric spaces.

status_evidence.title: From topology to metric: modal logic and quantification in metric spaces
status_evidence.snippet: For finite subspaces of the real line and higher-dimensional Euclidean spaces, undecidability of MS-satisfiability is established via reduction from Diophantine equations.
status_evidence.claim: Full MS is undecidable over Euclidean subspaces, motivating the study of fragments which remains open.
